crosswalks.historical_boundary: UNESCO Great Zimbabwe National Monument archaeological property, approximately 800 ha, with the fourteenth-century Great Enclosure and continuously occupied Hill Ruins; this is the site boundary and not the surrounding Victoria District or the wider Zimbabwe state.
crosswalks.resolution_method: Use the dedicated EU5 great_zimbabwe location whose historical name and calibrated geography identify the containing location. Because the evidence is a one-sided floor for an archaeological site, the full containing location is constrained to support at least 10,000 people; no fraction of the coarse EU5 capacity is assigned to the site and no surrounding rural population is added.
crosswalks.notes: The coarse EU5 footprint is much larger than the approximately 800 ha archaeological property. This is intentionally conservative for a lower-bound inequality, but the area ratio is preserved so it cannot be mistaken for an area-complete regional target.
